title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and multiplicative structures. The previous page mentions a De Rham–Sullivan complex, so the setting is rational-homotopy-style multiplicative structures. This page introduces an axiomatic notion of a 'catégorie polynômiale'. The aim seems to be a framework in which non-linear (polynomial) operations, such as products and cup-product-type maps, live alongside linear ones and can be split into homogeneous components.

Definition. A polynomial category is a category P with a wide, generally non-full subcategory P_1 of 'admissible' (linear) arrows such that:
(a) P has finite products.
(b) Ob P_1 = Ob P, so P_1 is given by a set Fl_1 ⊂ Fl(P) containing the identities and closed under composition. Products in P are also products in P_1: an arrow u = (v,w): Z → X×Y is admissible iff its components v, w are. A struck clause asks that X → e (terminal) be admissible.
(c) P_1 is an additive category.

Consequences drawn on the page.
- Every object, with its P_1-biproduct structure maps (which are admissible), is an abelian group object in P_1 and hence in P, because the products coincide.
- So each Hom_P(X,Y) is an abelian group, natural in X but not in Y. Composition is right-distributive, (f+g)∘h = f∘h + g∘h, but not left-distributive in general: f∘(g+h) ≠ f∘g + f∘h. Left-distributivity holds when f is admissible.
- Z maps to End(id_{P_1}), sending n to n·id. The multiplicative monoid Z^× therefore acts by the admissible endomorphisms n·id_X. This gives an action on P(X,Y) by μ_n(f) = f∘(n·id), i.e. precomposition with scalar multiplication.

The next page adds axiom (d): a grading P(X,Y) = ⊕_{n≥0} P_n(X,Y) with f_n∘(λ id_X) = λ^n f_n. There is also a multi-graded version for P(X_1×…×X_r, Y), indexed by multidegrees and with the analogous multihomogeneity. Grothendieck starts, then strikes, a uniqueness lemma for such weight decompositions under a (Z^×)^r action.

In modern terms this is a cartesian 'left additive' category, with a chosen wide subcategory of linear maps forming an additive category with the same products, together with a decomposition of all maps into homogeneous polynomial components. The model is polynomial maps between abelian groups or modules: the scaling λ acts on degree-n homogeneous parts by λ^n. This weight decomposition is the kind used for Adams-type operations, or Sullivan's grading automorphisms, on multiplicative structures.
errors: The action is written μ_n(f) = f∘(n id_Y). For f: X → Y the meaningful action is precomposition f∘(n id_X). Postcomposition (n id_Y)∘f equals n·f, since n id_Y is admissible and hence additive. This also matches the next page, f_n∘(λ id_X) = λ^n f_n. Probably a slip of index.

The arrow End(id_P) → End(id_{P_1}) is ambiguous. The transformation n·id is natural only with respect to admissible maps, so in general it does not lie in End(id_P). The correct statement is that Z → End(id_{P_1}) and Z^× acts by these admissible endomorphisms.

The terminal-object condition (X → e admissible, i.e. e is the zero object of P_1) is struck. It is needed, or follows only if one reads 'finite products' to include the empty product preserved in P_1. The text leaves this implicit.

Gap on the next page: the uniqueness of the weight decomposition fails without torsion hypotheses. gcd_λ(λ^n − λ^{n'}) can be > 1; e.g. λ^2 − λ is always even. So with 2-torsion, as with Frobenius-type maps over F_2, degrees 1 and 2 cannot be separated by the Z^× action. The lemma Grothendieck began, and struck, needs Hom groups that are torsion-free, or uniquely divisible by the relevant integers.

ideas.what: Category with finite products whose hom-sets are abelian groups with only right-distributivity, and a wide subcategory of 'linear' maps (left-distributive) that is additive with the same products
ideas.modern_name: Cartesian left additive category (with chosen subcategory of additive/linear maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Blute–Cockett–Seely, 'Cartesian differential categories' (2009); earlier analogues in near-ring / non-additive category literature

ideas.what: Every object is an abelian group object since products in P agree with biproducts in additive P_1; Hom_P(X,Y) is natural in X only
ideas.modern_name: Enrichment of a cartesian category over abelian groups via group objects; left additivity

ideas.what: Action of the multiplicative monoid Z^× by precomposition with n·id, and decomposition of maps into homogeneous components of degree n (λ ↦ λ^n), multigraded for multi-variable maps
ideas.modern_name: Weight/degree decomposition of polynomial maps; homogeneous polynomial functors; Adams-type weight eigenspaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–MacLane (polynomial functors, 1954); Friedlander–Suslin (strict polynomial functors, 1997); Adams operations weight decompositions

missed.claim: Around 1975–76 Grothendieck axiomatizes exactly the structure later called a cartesian left additive category. The left additive structure has a designated additive wide subcategory with the same products, and he explicitly notes right- but not left-distributivity. He then enriches it with a degree grading by homogeneous polynomial components. This predates Blute–Cockett–Seely (2009) by over 30 years, and the grading by scalar action is a feature not part of their axioms.
missed.quote: (i.e. on a (f+g)∘h = f∘h + g∘h) mais non nécessairement f∘(g+h) ≠ f∘g + f∘h !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Cartesian differential/tangent category theory studies left additive categories and polynomial or Taylor expansions. An axiomatic 'polynomial category' with graded homogeneous components is a natural intermediate notion. The motivation here, multiplicative structures on cochain complexes à la De Rham–Sullivan, suggests applications to rational homotopy and power operations that this literature has not linked to Grothendieck.

missed.claim: The program of using polynomial categories to handle multiplicative structures on ∂-perfect complexes is left at the definition stage. The uniqueness of the weight decomposition is begun and struck, apparently because of torsion issues.
missed.quote: c) P_1 est une catégorie additive
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Weight decompositions under scaling are central in rational homotopy formality (grading automorphisms) and in λ-ring/Adams operation theory. An integral, non-additive categorical framework for them, with its torsion obstructions, is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean early definition of what is now a cartesian left additive category, plus a polynomial grading, appears here unpublished and uncredited. However, it is only a definition with elementary consequences, and similar non-additive structures were known informally.
transcription_corrections: The title is underlined and partly illegible; the first word is 'Catégories' and it ends in '...ynômiales'. There may be a prefix before 'polynômiales'.
The struck marginal note at the top refers to P_1(X,Y) and 'P(X,Y)'. It is a deleted condition, not part of the final axioms.
The diagram reads 'Z → End(id_{P_1}) ← End(id_P)', and later 'Z^× → End(P_1) ← End(P)' as transcribed.
The last line indeed reads 'μ_n(f) = f∘(n id_Y)' in the image, mathematically presumably id_X.
